newsitem.title: USA: U.S. farm groups rally behind ethanol subsidy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. farm groups rally behind ethanol subsidy.

text.p: More than two dozen U.S. agricultural groups asked House Speaker Newt Gingrich and Democratic leader Dick Gephardt on Monday to save the ethanol subsidy program from federal budget-cutters.

A letter from the American Farm Bureau, the National Corn Growers Association, the American Soybean Association, the National Association of Wheat Growers and 28 other groups protested a plan by House Ways and Means Chairman Bill Archer to eliminate the ethanol subsidy.
Cargill Inc, the big U.S. grain trading and processing company, also signed the letter.
"Numerous studies have demonstrated that the federal ethanol program is good for the economy, for the environment and for farmers and rural communities," the letter said.

"Tax incentives that promote the sale of ethanol-blended gasolines are building an important, value-added domestic energy industry, just as federal incentives aided the development of the U.S. oil and gas industries," it said.

Ethanol is made from corn and other grain feedstocks. Ethanol producers that blend gasoline with it can claim a 5.4 cent per gallon exemption on the current excise tax of 18.4 cents per gallon as part of a measure authorized by Congress through the year 2000.

Archer has repeatedly said he wants to repeal the ethanol tax break to help balance the federal budget. Farm groups are worried that Archer's plan could succeed this year because of the retirement of Sen. Robert Dole of Kansas, the former majority leader, who had backed the ethanol subsidy.
